notes:
1. One Schedules page

Automation → Schedules now has three tabs:
All schedules: every scheduled job and background task.
Report & command jobs: what used to be the Scheduled jobs page.
Setup & health: what used to be Background tasks.
The two old pages are gone from the sidebar. Links, GAMbit roles and Helper answers that mention them now open the right tab.
Why “GAMbit job - Assigned users” didn’t appear: most likely its saved settings were lost (probably in the broken update) while the Windows task stayed behind, and the page couldn’t recognise it.
What fixes it:
GAMbit now reads what each Windows task actually runs, so every task in its Task Scheduler folder is listed.
A task whose settings are missing shows as Saved job (settings missing). Select it and click Edit… to set it up again (it keeps the same task), or Delete it.
A new Windows task column shows the exact name you see in Task Scheduler, so you can match them up.

2. Activity log shows what was done

New “What was done” column: Chromebook changes now read like “Chromebook 5CD0372JK1 (asset HS2074): moved to /Chrome Devices/Elementary School”.
The command column shows serial numbers in brackets, like gam cros [5CD0372JK1] update ou …. Copy command, Run again and Undo still use the exact original command.
Batch changes: hover over the row to see every Chromebook it changed. Export… includes that list.
Other changes read the same way, for example “Suspended jdoe@…” or “Added … to staff@…”.
Older entries show serials too, as long as GAMbit has listed those Chromebooks at least once. Loading the fleet once fills that in for every device.

3. Load Chromebooks covers the whole fleet page

The button at the top now fetches everything the tabs need in one go.
Assigned users fills in and shows its preview straight away, including when it’s limited to certain org units.
Assignment sync, Redistribution, Asset register and Withdrawn students’ devices use the same list, so their buttons answer instantly. Each of them still needs its own input, like a spreadsheet, so they don’t start by themselves.
No stale data: any change GAMbit makes to Chromebooks clears the list, and it expires after an hour. Click Load Chromebooks again whenever you want the latest from Google.
Still loaded separately: Health, Apps & extensions, Printers and Battery forecast, because they need detailed device reports the main list doesn’t include.
